newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Kabul's main food and fuel supply route reopened.
newsitem.headline: Kabul's main food and fuel supply route reopened.

text.p: One of Kabul's main supply routes reopened on Tuesday after a one-day closure caused by fighting between government forces and Islamic Taleban rebels, witnesses said.
They said Kabul-bound trucks laden with firewood and fuel were plying the road from the Taleban-held town of Maidan Shahr, about 30 km (19 miles) southwest of the Afghan capital.
The road was closed on Monday when government troops launched a ground assault on Taleban positions near Arghandi, about 20 km (13 miles) southwest of Kabul.
A Taleban spokesman said the attack had been repelled.
The Taleban, entrenched in hills south of Kabul for the past year, have sworn to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani and impose strict Islamic rule throughout Afghanistan.
